question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 26 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The deployment of a new search version caused the increase in latency and request volume.
why_chain: The deployment of search v3.1 led to a spike in request volume and increased latency.
The increased request volume overwhelmed the autoscaler, which triggered scaling out.
The scaling out process took time, causing a delay in response times.

contributing_factors.description: The config change to the checkout feature flag likely contributed to the increase in latency.
why_chain: The new_ui_flow feature flag change introduced a new path in the checkout process.
This new path may have introduced inefficiencies or bugs that affected latency.
The increased request volume due to the flash sale campaign exacerbated the issue.

contributing_factors.description: The flash sale campaign likely caused the spike in request volume and error rate.
why_chain: The flash sale campaign led to a sudden increase in user traffic.
This increased traffic overwhelmed the system, leading to higher request volume and error rates.
The autoscaler scaling out process coincided with the flash sale campaign, further straining the system.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The autoscaler scaling out was the main cause.
ruled_out.reason: The autoscaler scaling out happened after the change, not before.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate increase was due to a bug in the new search version.
ruled_out.reason: The error rate increase is correlated with the deployment of the new search version, but not caused by it.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The config change was the main cause.
ruled_out.reason: The config change happened before the deployment, not after.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region eu-west rose from 137 ms to 224 ms (+64%), with a change point at 2026-03-26T13:45:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region eu-west: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.02).
At the same time, request volume for region eu-west rose (2118 per 5 min before, 7734 per 5 min after, +265%).
At the same time, error rate for region eu-west rose (0.48% before, 0.97% after, +102%).
Changed checkout feature flag new_ui_flow to 50% in eu-west (checkout, eu-west; 3 min before the change; record R016)
Marketing: flash sale campaign goes live in eu-west at 13:45 UTC (eu-west; 220 min before the change; record R014)
Request volume 3x normal in eu-west (eu-west; 12 min after the change; record R017)
Deployed search v3.1 to eu-west (routine release) (search, eu-west; 136 min before the change; record R015)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (eu-west; 20 min after the change; record R018)

reasons: ✗ The closest change event is 136 min before the change, too far to be convincing.
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✗ Request volume also rose, so a traffic explanation is still open.
✗ 2 other change event(s) fit about as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
missing_data: Change records from the hour before the change
Details to tell the competing changes apart (e.g. a rollback test)

actions.action: Roll back the search v3.1 deployment to eu-west.
Monitor the checkout feature flag and rollback if issues arise.
Prepare for future flash sale campaigns by increasing capacity and optimizing the checkout process.
